title: Hampton changing arrangements and Quincy Jones
summary: Love for Sale arranged by Quincy Jones kept being altered by Hampton.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I'm wondering when you moved from one band to another, when you came back, was it hard to get in the groove of that band? I mean, to get back to the material? Mm-hmm. Or was it, were the bands fairly repetitious? In other words, did Hampton have a certain stock set of arrangements, stock set of songs? Mm-hmm. Or did he change? He changed.
So when you came, if you left Hampton and came back six months later or a year?

Oh, now the one thing that, one number that really hurted me was when the change was that, his own one of the albums, Love for Sale. Mm-hmm. Quincy Jones wrote that, Quincy was with the band, and that was one of his first arrangements he wrote for a big band. Mm-hmm. And every time, every month, he would take something out and put something in until he just changed the whole arrangement.
Mm-hmm. So you didn't like what Quincy had done? No, I liked what Quincy had done.
I didn't like the idea of Hampton changing it.
